questions.q: Which Quad X motor does Betaflight write to the log as `motor[2]`?
options: Rear right (motor 1)
Front right (motor 2)
Rear left (motor 3)
Front left (motor 4)
questions.explain: The numbering is 1 RR, 2 FR, 3 RL, 4 FL, and the log indices start from zero: motor[2] is motor 3, the rear left (mixerQuadX[] in flight/mixer_init.c).

options: Reverses the motor rotation over DShot
Inverts the sign of the yaw PID before the mixer
Mirrors the motor numbers
Reorders the motor outputs on the pads
questions.explain: In mixTable() the sign of scaledAxisPidYaw changes with this flag; the mixer table, the numbers and the actual motor rotation stay the same — the direction is changed in the ESC.

questions.q: The log header has `motorOutput:158,2047`, and the median of `motor[0]` = 1102. What is that in percent of travel?
questions.explain: p = (1102 − 158)/(2047 − 158)·100 = 944/1889·100 = 50.0 %. 52.7 % comes out if the range 48,2047 is used (that happens only with dynamic idle), and 53.8 % — if 1102 is divided by 2047 without subtracting the lower limit.

questions.q: Why is the imbalance computed from the median of the segment, not the mean?
options: The median is robust to gusts and one-off corrections
A mean cannot be computed from integer DShot values
Blackbox records the motors only once a second
The median accounts for the motorOutput header by itself
questions.explain: The motor output jumps all the time from PID corrections; one gust of wind shifts the mean and hardly touches the median.

questions.q: The indices: I_pitch = +4.5 %, I_roll = +0.3 %, I_yaw = −0.2 %. The most likely cause?
options: A weak motor 4 (front left)
One motor is tilted tangentially
The CG is offset to the rear
Different timing on two ESCs
questions.explain: Pitch alone with zero yaw is the signature of an offset CG: the rear motors carry more. A weak motor would give three indices of the same magnitude, a tilt — only yaw.

questions.q: The indices are roughly equal: I_pitch ≈ −3 %, I_roll ≈ +3 %, I_yaw ≈ +3 %. What does this point to first of all?
options: A center of gravity offset to the left
One corner: motor 4 FL or its prop
A wrong `yaw_motors_reversed`
A yaw I term that is too low
questions.explain: Three indices of the same magnitude ≈ w/2 with the signs “front, left, diagonal 1+4” are the pattern of the single corner FL. Whether it is the motor or the prop is decided by the swap test.

questions.q: A constant I_yaw of 7 % with I_pitch and I_roll near zero. Swapping the props and the motors does not move the imbalance. What should be checked?
options: Raise yaw P and I
Change `motor_output_reordering`
Enable `thrust_linear`
The tilt of the motor axes and the straightness of the arms
questions.explain: Pure yaw that does not move with the parts is a torque from the geometry: a motor tilted tangentially by ~1° on a 10" gives, by the module's estimate, on the order of 7–13 % in terms of the command.

questions.q: Why, in the lab, is log B recorded after motors 1 and 4 are swapped?
options: To check the motor order in the Motors tab
So that the CG shifts and the pitch index goes to zero
No mass was moved: the correct hypothesis keeps the CG
So that the diagonal imbalance changes sign
questions.explain: From one log, “motor 4 + CG rearward” and “motor 1 + CG sideways” describe the medians equally well. After the swap the CG is the same, so the correct hypothesis is the one whose CG estimate did not change (0.3 % against 12.3 %).
